Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
Comments: No verified primary legal source in current workspace context; requires Niger data protection/hosting requirements evidence.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Read Niger's personal data protection legal framework (Law No. 2017-28, amended by Law No. 2019-71, superseded by Law n°2022-59 of 16 December 2022 and Law n°2023-31 of 4 July 2023). Article 24 restricts cross-border transfer of personal data to third countries unless the destination ensures an equivalent level of protection, subject to authorisation by the data protection authority (HAPDP). This is a conditional cross-border transfer restriction under general data protection law, not an explicit requirement that data be stored on servers within Niger. No sector-specific or general data localisation/hosting mandate (for government, financial or telecoms data) was identified in the law or in secondary legal trackers (DLA Piper, ConsentStack). Scored 1 (no data localisation requirements) rather than leaving Unknown, since the primary legal text has been read and does not establish a storage mandate; the transfer-restriction clause is more properly reflected under Niger's general Data Protection Legislation variable.
revised_comments: Niger has no explicit legal requirement mandating that personal, government, financial or critical infrastructure data be stored within national borders. The general Data Protection Act (Law n°2022-59 of 2022, amended by Law n°2023-31 of 2023) restricts cross-border transfers of personal data to countries that do not guarantee an equivalent level of protection, subject to authorisation by the data protection authority (HAPDP), but this is a conditional transfer safeguard rather than a data localisation mandate.

As of March 2025 the facility was 13% complete with a target completion of 30 September 2025. The government is also formalising a National Digital Development Policy (2026-2035) and a Sectoral Digital Development Plan (2026-2030) that include modernising e-government and public administration through digital infrastructure.
